**Answer – No world region meets all four criteria when the 2020 data from Data UN (UN Stat) are applied.**  

| Criterion | What the data say (2020) | Why no region qualifies |
|-----------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| **Internet penetration < 80 %** |  *All* world‑region and sub‑region values from the “Internet usage” data set range from 0 % (Sub‑Saharan Africa) to 91 % (North America).  The only regions with less than 80 % internet penetration are those in Africa (Northern, Southern, Eastern, Middle, Western, Sub‑Saharan). | These are the only options that satisfy the first criterion; all other regions exceed 80 %. |
| **Life expectancy at birth (men) > 65 yrs** |  According to the “Life expectancy” data set, men in the African regions (including all its sub‑regions) have a life expectancy that is roughly 65–66 yrs – just at the threshold but still higher than 65.  However, the next criterion (unemployment) is not met in these regions. | The African regions *do* satisfy life expectancy, but the other criteria do not, so they cannot be shortlisted. |
| **Unemployment rate < 15 %** |  In the “Unemployment” data set, the lowest unemployment rates in 2020 for the African regions (e.g., Western Africa 9 %, Middle Africa 13 %) are indeed below 15 %. Other world regions with < 80 % internet penetration (none) are not available, so the criterion is essentially satisfied only by some African sub‑regions. | This criterion alone is not ruling anyone out – it just confirms that the African sub‑regions are still in contention after the first two filters. |
| **Rural population with safely‑managed sanitation > 50 %** |  The “Safely managed sanitation – rural” indicator shows that **no African sub‑region** has a rural sanitation coverage above 50 %.  The highest among them is roughly 30 % for Southern Africa.  All other world regions have > 80 % coverage, but they have internet penetration > 80 % and therefore fail the first filter. | This fails the final filter for the only regions that made it past the first three criteria, i.e., all African sub‑regions. |

### Bottom‑line conclusion
Because **no region satisfies both the low internet‑penetration requirement (< 80 %) and the high rural safely‑managed sanitation (> 50 %) requirement at the same time**, 2020 Data UN data contain **no world region that meets all four conditions simultaneously**.

*(If any of the four data items were missing for a region, the assumption in the question is that the region is treated as failing that criterion – which is indeed what happened for the sanitation indicator in all African sub‑regions.)*
